title: The coordinator's state machine as a LangGraph graph: its own actions as nodes, the person as pauses, nothing replaced
request: Phase 6 (the owner): a multi-agent system on an orchestration layer that enhances, never replaces, what exists; 28.3: the orchestrator.
plan: One node situates the draft with the coordinator's own situation; it alone chooses the next node.
One node per action calls the coordinator's act unchanged.
The person is reached through pauses: a question, a confirmation, an approval.
Every node advances the board; a walk's record kept.
Measure the dev journeys through the graph against the loop.

decisions.decision: The graph calls Coordinator.act and where unchanged; the loop stays the path with no framework.
decisions.why: The owner: enhance, never replace; one set of rules decides what comes next whichever path walks it.

decisions.decision: An answer carries the key of the pause it was given to.
decisions.why: A draft can change while a walk waits (the person answers in the chat, the map is redrawn); an answer must never be taken for another question.

decisions.decision: After an approval the draft is situated again before the build.
decisions.why: The approval may wait for hours; what was true before it is not evidence after it.

decisions.decision: A pause is not a failed harness step; it is closed on the board, answered or declined.
decisions.why: The traces are training data: a pause recorded as an error teaches the wrong thing.

change: dclab_rnd/orchestra/walk.py (Walk, Asker, drive, the critic's nodes of 28.4); the harness's timed step lets a pause through; board.record emits team.recorded; deleting a draft deletes its checkpoints; the journeys' --walk graph stored as the arm rules_graph; agent orchestra.walk.

findings.defect: The build ran on a situation read before the approval's pause.
findings.scenario: The walk paused for the build's approval; the page's Build button built the draft meanwhile; resuming built a second project for the one draft.
findings.cause: The node acted on the situation computed before the pause; the build's own checks did not refuse a built draft.
findings.fix: After the approval the draft is situated again; the walk builds only when the situation still says build.

findings.defect: A resumed answer was recorded against whatever question was open at the resume.
findings.scenario: The walk paused on the outcome; the person answered it in the chat, so the moment became the open question; resuming with the outcome's words recorded them as the prediction moment.
findings.cause: LangGraph re-runs the node on resume and hands the stored answer to the first pause whatever it now asks.
findings.fix: Each pause carries a key of what it asks; the answer is wrapped with the key of the pause shown; a different key asks again.

findings.defect: Every pause was recorded as a failed harness step, and a declined build was not recorded.
findings.scenario: Each question wrote a step with error GraphInterrupt, then the same step again on resume; a declined build left no step and no closed pause.
findings.cause: The interrupt raised inside the harness's timed block.
findings.fix: The harness lets LangGraph's interrupt through without a step; the decline and the approval are steps; every pause is closed on the board, answered or declined, with its event.

findings.defect: The walk's record missed its pauses, spend, time and start, and was no event.
findings.scenario: A walk with nine pauses recorded 0 interrupts, 0 spend, every node 0 seconds, and a start equal to its end.
findings.cause: The board held only closed pauses, which the walk never wrote; the start was taken at the end.
findings.fix: The start kept in the walk's state at its first invoke; the pauses closed on the board; the spend from the model requests of the walk's sessions; each node's seconds; team.recorded emitted.

findings.defect: Deleting a draft left its walk's checkpoints, with the person's answers.
findings.scenario: After retention.forget, the SQLite checkpoints still held the resumed answers of the draft's thread.
findings.cause: Retention removed the orchestra files only.
findings.fix: forget deletes the thread's checkpoints (SQLite or PostgreSQL), opened only where a walk ever ran.

findings.defect: The board after a node showed the draft before it.
findings.scenario: After the build the board said state build, not built.
findings.cause: The board was computed from the situation before the action.
findings.fix: The board after a node reads the draft after it.

findings.defect: Resume, the approval window, a changed question and retention had no tests; parity covered 3 of the 15 journeys.
findings.scenario: A broken resume would have passed.
findings.cause: Tests drove one Walk object in one process.
findings.fix: Tests for each; the 15 dev journeys run through the graph and stored as a result.

measurements.name: the dev journeys through the graph (JRN-010)
measurements.gate: 15 of 15 dev journeys right through the graph, as through the loop, with no move refused by the validator
measurements.result: 15 of 15 right on the card, the workflow, the pipeline and the holdout (95% interval 0.796 to 1.0), 0 moves refused, the critic's rules on; stored as the arm rules_graph
limits: Written journeys over seeded replicas: the same rules decide in both walks, so parity says the graph changes nothing, not that it is better.

outcome: The coordinator's walk runs as a graph that pauses for the person and resumes from its checkpoint, with every step, pause and spend recorded, and nothing of the coordinator rewritten.
lessons: A framework that re-runs a node on resume makes every value read before a pause stale: read again after it.
Give each pause an identity; an answer is to a question, not to a position in a node.
risks: The product's Home still walks the loop: the graph serves after 28.8.
